answer: Reciprocal neighbor overlap. Each agent must maintain a distinct set of counterparties whose own neighbor sets overlap its own above a fixed threshold, forming a slowly shifting nebula of mutual links. An identity whose neighbors never cite it back fails the overlap test and is dropped from routing. To pass, an attacker must build real two-way links across many agents, and that tide of reciprocal traffic costs sustained attention per identity, not a one-time payment. Honest clusters grow like a river widening downstream, while fabricated ones stay thin.
